text:
The doctor is good, but the counter service isn't very good. I took my boyfriend today. The appointment was for 8 PM, but yesterday we called to inquire about earlier slots because my boyfriend recently moved, about 24 km from the clinic. We wanted to reschedule for Monday if there weren't any available slots. My boyfriend emphasized that they were indeed available, not just walk-in appointments, and the clinic staff said there was a 5 PM slot. He stressed that they said 5 PM was available, not a walk-in slot. So we agreed to that time. Upon arrival today, after the medical history check, my boyfriend mentioned that the 5 PM slot we called yesterday was cancelled. The counter staff said there were no available slots, and he was asked if he wanted to wait (referring to walk-in appointments). My boyfriend repeated that they said there were no available slots, only walk-in appointments. He asked how long the wait would be, and the staff replied that the first case alone took 30 minutes, and there were many customers waiting (the tone was very unpleasant). My boyfriend said he wouldn't wait because it was too far. He then got up to leave. The staff member shouted, "Next time, make an appointment a month in advance, not just a week!" (The tone was extremely unpleasant). I'm a very calm person; I didn't argue or speak up, but today I think they've had enough, having tolerated this staff member's tone many times before.

1. I went because the clinic staff said there were available slots. If there were a last-minute appointment, why would I ask to change the time? If I did, I'd still have to wait 1-2 hours anyway. Wouldn't it be better to go to the original 8 PM appointment? They said one thing on the phone and another at the counter. I emphasize again, the tone was extremely unpleasant and unacceptable. The way they shouted at me at the end was awful. At the very least, as a service employee, you should speak to customers more politely. Tone can be adjusted. Whether there are available slots or not, you should speak more respectfully, especially in a service job. I'm paying for this service; I'm not asking for it for free.

However, I want to emphasize that the doctor is excellent. The only issue is the counter staff. Please improve that.
